recent_items.title: BitGo CEO Mike Belshe says digital assets are going mainstream, with or without Congress
recent_items.summary:
On October 7, 2026, BitGo co-founder and CEO Mike Belshe told Bloomberg at Token2049 in Singapore that digital assets are joining the mainstream financial system 'whether the US Congress acts or not,' framing adoption as advancing regardless of what US lawmakers do. Token2049 Singapore runs October 7 to 8, and Belshe is scheduled to appear on the Institutional Stage on October 8 for a session on what regulatory clarity means for institutional strategy in crypto.

Around the interview, the article points to BitGo's Asia-Pacific expansion. The company's Singapore trading desk is now its largest anywhere in the world, according to the report. BitGo, which trades publicly under the ticker BTGO, ties that growth to the Major Payment Institution licence it obtained in 2024, reporting that its APAC client base has tripled since the licence was granted, regional headcount has more than doubled, and regional trading volumes more than doubled in the first half of 2026.

The article also notes that on October 6, during the Token2049 window, BitGo and HashKey Cloud formalized a strategic partnership spanning staking, trading, custody, and real-world asset tokenization, which the report describes as deepening BitGo's regional ties.

Separately, the report notes Belshe has positioned prime brokerage as BitGo's target revenue driver, with a stated aim for prime brokerage to become 100% of revenue rather than relying on standalone custody fees, and says the HashKey deal's service mix fits into that vision as the article frames it.

For readers following BTGO, the article closes by framing the company's story as increasingly about Asia and revenue mix, holding up Singapore's licensing framework as a practical example of how a defined regulatory regime can attract institutional business. The piece was edited by John Chen, per its disclosure.

recent_items.title: BitGo Bank & Trust brings Lido ETH staking to eligible US clients
recent_items.summary: On October 7, 2026, BitGo Bank & Trust, N.A. announced that eligible US clients can stake Ether through Lido directly inside their existing BitGo accounts, with staking, the stETH receipt and ongoing position management handled in one place, according to a Crypto Briefing report. Clients stake ETH and receive stETH, Lido's liquid staking token, which represents a staked position and remains transferable while the underlying ETH stays staked; the approach avoids traditional lock-up periods, per the article's explainer. The report says BitGo's US clients will not need to set up extra operational workflows or bring in additional counterparties, and it describes BitGo as positioned to be the first US-based qualified custodian to offer native ETH staking through Lido, a first-mover characterization attributed to the companies. Kean Gilbert, Head of Institutional Relations at the Lido Ecosystem Foundation, framed the move as supplying the custodial backing institutions need to pursue Lido staking strategies. Nathan Stump, Managing Director at BitGo, emphasized keeping BitGo's controls in place while letting the service plug into clients' existing asset management infrastructure. Figures cited in the report put BitGo's custody platform at more than $100 billion in digital assets, of which $48 billion is designated as staked, and Lido at more than $25 billion in staked ETH — over 25% of all staked ETH and the leading liquid staking protocol by market share. Per the article, the US launch builds on a July 2025 rollout that connected BitGo clients in Europe and Asia to Lido's staking services, giving the two companies more than a year of operating history before extending the offer to US clients. It describes the most direct impact as falling on US institutions already custodying ETH with BitGo, which can pursue staking yield through Lido without changing custodians or rebuilding their operational stack, and suggests the regulated US distribution channel could reinforce Lido's lead while giving rival custodians a benchmark to neutralize. Separately from this announcement, BitGo had other institutional news in the same week per prior reports — an October 6 partnership signing between BitGo and HashKey Cloud covering staking, trading, custody and tokenization, and an October 5 Grayscale 8-K naming BitGo Bank & Trust an additional custodian for its Hyperliquid Staking ETF — but the report does not connect either to this launch. The companies did not disclose staking fees, detailed eligibility criteria or an availability timeline in the report.

recent_items.title: BitGo and HashKey expand institutional partnership
recent_items.summary: On October 6, 2026, at 08:00 UTC, BitGo Holdings and HashKey Cloud announced a strategic partnership covering staking, trading, custody and real-world asset tokenization for eligible institutional clients in Asia-Pacific. The companies signed the agreement at the Fullerton Bay Hotel in Singapore during TOKEN2049 week. BitGo signed with WanCloud Ltd., the HashKey Group company that operates as HashKey Cloud. Abel Seow, BitGo's managing director and head of APAC sales, and Leo Li, CEO of HashKey OnChain BG, represented the companies at the ceremony. Per the announcement, the signing extends a staking collaboration the two companies began in July into a broader relationship. The agreement is divided into four service lines. HashKey Cloud will become a validator partner on BitGo's platform, with initial staking support covering Ethereum and Solana for eligible BitGo institutional clients; the release describes those two networks as the starting set without naming additional assets or a date for adding them. On custody, BitGo will make its custody services available to HashKey Capital and associated funds, subject to customary onboarding and separate agreements — the announcement establishes a framework and does not show that any fund's assets have moved into BitGo custody. For tokenized real-world assets, BitGo will become a custody partner for HashKey's initiatives, though the release names no asset, issuer, chain or planned issuance and does not specify whether BitGo would hold the underlying asset, the on-chain token, reserve assets or a combination. The trading component is the least defined: the companies said HashKey Cloud and BitGo will collaborate to support institutional trading flow, without identifying venues, settlement arrangements, order types, asset coverage or which entity would face each client. No transaction value or launch schedule was disclosed for any part of the agreement. The release limits every described service to eligible clients and jurisdictions where the activity is permitted, and provides no staking fee terms, validator performance standards, slashing allocation or withdrawal mechanics. HashKey Cloud describes itself as HashKey Holding's institutional staking and Web3 infrastructure arm, providing node validation services since 2018; BitGo says it operates multiple regulated entities, including BitGo Bank & Trust, National Association. The companies describe the combined offer as serving institutions across the asset lifecycle, while each workstream remains separately defined — the announcement does not say that HashKey Capital will use HashKey Cloud as validator, that trading clients must use BitGo custody, or that a tokenized asset must use the new staking connection.

recent_items.title: BitGo and HashKey Cloud expand staking partnership into trading, custody and RWA tokenization
recent_items.summary:
BitGo and HashKey Cloud have expanded their existing staking partnership into institutional trading, custody and real-world asset tokenization, according to a crypto.news report. BitGo said on Oct. 6 that the companies signed the expanded agreement in Singapore during TOKEN2049 week, with WanCloud Ltd. — which operates as HashKey Cloud within HashKey Group — signing with NYSE-listed BitGo Holdings. The agreement covers four business areas — staking, institutional trading flow, custody and real-world asset (RWA) tokenization — and services are limited to eligible institutional customers and jurisdictions where the relevant products are permitted. The report says the companies disclosed no financial terms, launch schedule, initial customers or expected assets under management.

Staking is the continuation of work the two companies had already begun. Their first partnership, announced in July, centered on institutional staking and was designed to let institutional clients participate in proof-of-stake networks while keeping their assets within BitGo's custody framework, with HashKey Cloud supplying the validator infrastructure. The new agreement makes HashKey Cloud a validator partner on BitGo's platform, with Ethereum and Solana as the first supported staking assets for eligible institutional clients. The article notes that neither company has given an exact date for expanded staking access or identified the first clients expected to use the service, and that the Oct. 6 announcement did not disclose fees, staking reward terms or how much ETH and SOL could enter the arrangement. HashKey Cloud has operated blockchain validation infrastructure since 2018, and its website lists staking products for institutions, asset managers and professional investors across multiple blockchain networks.

On trading, the companies said they will work together to support institutional trading flow, though the announcement did not identify exchanges, trading pairs or expected volumes. Per the report, BitGo already runs trading and settlement infrastructure alongside its custody business, its Singapore entity holds a Major Payment Institution license covering digital payment token services and cross-border money transfers according to the Monetary Authority of Singapore's financial institutions register, and BitGo recently expanded an off-exchange settlement arrangement with OKX under which supported assets can remain in segregated custody at BitGo Singapore while eligible institutions outside the U.S. access exchange liquidity. The article states that the HashKey agreement does not say that same setup will automatically apply to the new trading relationship.

Custody terms are more specific: BitGo will make its custody services available to HashKey Capital and associated funds, subject to client onboarding and separate agreements. The report cites BitGo platform figures for the end of June — 5,833 clients, $65.2 billion in assets on the platform, $11.9 billion in assets staked and second-quarter staking revenue of $64.7 million.

On real-world assets, BitGo will serve as a custody partner for HashKey's tokenization initiatives across Asia-Pacific markets. The report relays HashKey's first-half 2026 figures — HK$2.68 billion in onchain RWA total value locked, up 167.8% from a year earlier, with institutional customers accounting for HK$231.5 billion of its HK$282.2 billion platform trading volume, or 82% — and says HashKey's tokenization work has included regulated products in Hong Kong, a recent move by HashKey Exchange to distribute Franklin Templeton's tokenized U.S. government money market fund to eligible professional investors, and a September arrangement with Prometheum Capital and Velocity Capital covering a proposed route for tokenized U.S. equities that remains subject to final agreements, regulatory clearance and technical work. The report presents those items as HashKey's existing activity rather than as components of the BitGo agreement.

Abel Seow, BitGo's managing director and head of APAC sales, said institutions in Asia are seeking infrastructure covering several stages of digital asset activity. Leo Li, CEO of HashKey OnChain BG, described the combination of HashKey's Hong Kong presence and BitGo's custody infrastructure as a 'trusted pathway across staking, trading, custody, and tokenization.'

The report situates the agreement within both companies' wider positioning. It notes BitGo completed its acquisition of NYDIG's institutional trading business on Aug. 27, bringing in derivatives, financing, execution and structured-product capabilities along with roughly 30 NYDIG employees and institutional client relationships, and that BitGo CEO Mike Belshe has said he wants prime brokerage to become the company's main revenue engine. BitGo reported $4.33 billion in second-quarter revenue, largely from digital asset sales, against $4.29 billion in direct costs and a $19 million net loss, with management saying custody and wallet relationships remain the foundation for selling clients several products. HashKey, which listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in December 2025 under stock code 3887, reported first-half platform trading volume up 31.8% year over year and institutional trading volume up 58.8%.

The article does not name initial institutional customers, provide a rollout schedule or disclose expected trading, staking or custody volumes. BitGo's custody services for HashKey Capital and its associated funds remain subject to customary onboarding and applicable agreements, and access to each service depends on local law and regulatory requirements.

last_published.angle: Apple has cleared China's AI regulators and is reportedly planning a December rollout of Apple Intelligence, ending a two-year feature blackout in one of its most important markets.
last_published.title: Apple's AI is reportedly coming to China in December
last_published.content_full:
Apple reportedly plans to switch on its first AI features in China in December, ending a two-year wait since Apple Intelligence and the upgraded Siri reached the US.

Two approvals opened the door. China's cyberspace regulator registered Apple's generative AI service in July — the only foreign company on that list — and on October 14 the industry ministry added Apple Intelligence models to permits covering the upcoming iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro. The filings also name Alibaba's Qwen, a nod to Apple's partnership with Alibaba on language models.

The stakes sit in one of Apple's most important markets, where second-quarter shipments rose 24.4% year over year, making Apple the number two phone seller behind Huawei.

The December date is a report, not an Apple announcement. Watch for confirmation, the Chinese feature lineup, and how the launch lines up with the new iPhones.
last_published.content_small: Two Chinese approvals — including the sole foreign spot on the cyberspace regulator's generative AI registration list — reportedly set up a December debut of Apple Intelligence in China, nearly two years after the features launched in the US.

recent_items.title: PENDLE drops nearly 10% as longs absorb 27x the liquidation losses of shorts and on-chain activity slides
recent_items.summary:
PENDLE traded down nearly 10% over the trailing 24 hours at press time on October 7, 2026, in a decline AMBCrypto attributed to perpetual capital flows and declining on-chain activity, while leaving open the possibility that the move could prove to be a stop hunt followed by a rebound.

The report described heavy selling pressure, pointing to a lopsided liquidation gap over the past 24 hours: long positions lost roughly $261,000 while shorts lost about $9,660 — a disparity the article characterized as longs losing 27 times more capital than shorts, a condition it linked to strongly bearish momentum favoring sellers. A Whale Retail Delta reading cited in the report indicated whales, rather than retail traders, were the more active participants during the decline, which the article read as whales responding to market conditions.

On-chain usage has weakened alongside the price. Per DeFiLlama data cited in the report, since September 25 the daily transaction count fell from 1,246 to roughly 667 — a decline of nearly 46% — and active addresses fell from 651 to roughly 387, down about 40.5%. The article suggested a drop of this scale often implies a significant reduction in the protocol's utility, putting the asset's performance at risk.

Despite that weakness, the report held out a bullish case: the funding rate stood at a positive 0.0032%, which the article interpreted as traders still positioning for a rally, and it argued that the large liquidation gap plus whale presence could be consistent with a stop hunt — a move that drives price into stop losses before reversing — meaning a rebound was not off the table. The article framed the stop-hunt scenario explicitly as a possibility rather than a confirmed outcome, and it identified no specific trigger for the selling.

All price, liquidation, whale-activity, funding-rate and on-chain figures come via the single AMBCrypto report and the data sources it cites, relayed without independent verification; the report gives no precise intraday timestamp for any of the readings beyond 'the past 24 hours' at press time.

last_published.title: Pendle Raises Looping Incentives to a $15M Cap Amid DeFi Rally
last_published.content_full:
Pendle Finance raised the cap on its PT Looping incentives program to $15 million for the August 17–27 window, per Crypto Briefing. last_published.angle: China's rebounding crude demand, driven by a fuel-export surge amid the Iran conflict, is the demand-side backdrop as prediction markets push up the odds of a crude all-time high by December.
last_published.title: China's August oil throughput rises as markets price a crude all-time high into year-end
last_published.content_full:
China's refineries ran harder in August. Oil throughput rose on a rebound in fuel exports, timed against the Iran conflict and the supply uncertainty it brings. As the world's largest crude importer, China's demand is a central driver of global crude prices, and this snapshot shows demand, not just geopolitics, pushing in that direction.

Prediction markets reflect it. The odds that crude reaches a fresh all-time high by the end of December sit near 16.5%, against just 1.9% for the same milestone by the end of September. The curve slopes sharply upward as the year stretches out.

That gap is the tension worth watching: near-term odds stay low while traders leave real room for a second-half spike. The open question is whether Chinese run-rates hold and Middle East supply strains persist — a pull in either direction would move that year-end number.
last_published.content_small: China's refineries ran harder in August on a fuel-export rebound, reinforcing the world's top importer as a driver of crude prices. Prediction markets now price a crude all-time high by December 31 at 16.5%, versus just 1.9% by the end of September.

last_published.angle: On-chain watchers flag a possible OTC distribution move by a wallet previously funded by Ethena's multisig.
last_published.title: Suspected Ethena-linked wallet sends $14M of ENA to FalconX
last_published.content_full:
A wallet believed to be linked to the Ethena team sent roughly 170 million ENA — about $14.09 million — to FalconX on Tuesday morning, according to Lookonchain and PANews, both citing X account @OnchainLens. The transfer is unconfirmed by either party.

Tokens flowing to FalconX, a major institutional OTC desk, often signal upcoming distribution or sales. Onchain Lens flagged the move as likely an OTC sale, but neither Ethena nor FalconX has commented publicly. The wallet's prior funding from Ethena's Gnosis Safe is the basis for the team-link attribution.

Watch for any Ethena statement clarifying the transfer's purpose, and whether ENA shows unusual trading activity in the hours ahead.
